title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of diabetes and kidney function.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been managed on an oral hypoglycemic for several years and reports consistent adherence to his regimen. He currently has a diagnosis of chronic kidney disease stage 4. The patient reports no new symptoms or acute concerns. He notes that his renal decline is not related to diabetes.

Medication List
Metformin 500mg BID
Glipizide 5mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no new skin lesions or acute musculoskeletal issues.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current oral medication.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: Stable; noted to be unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
1. Continue current metformin and glipizide regimen.
2. Continue monitoring renal function and laboratory work.
3. Return to clinic in three months for follow-up.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
